title: Opening excerpt: early records and the Ohio Lucky Seven
summary: Steiner introduces the 1961 interview excerpts; Davison recalls the Original Dixieland Jazz Band records and a 1921 dance in Ohio with the Ohio Lucky Seven.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I am John Steiner and these are excerpts of my interview with Bill Davison in November of 1961. Did you know the original Dixieland Jazz Band's records when you were a kid? Oh sure. You know them.
It's one they sold by the millions, why everybody must.

Yeah, oh everyone, yeah sure. In fact I have still have them all, I think the old ones you know. But I think the most exciting time for me of course, I once was, when I was with the Ohio Lucky Seven, which is the first band, this is 1921, I played in a spot in Ohio that had a girls college, Miami school for girls, and we played in the auditorium, or no, the basketball, where they played basketball. The gymnasium. Yeah. And we, the Ohio Lucky Seven was on one side of the hall, and on the other side, I didn't know. Yeah.
The New Yorker 17, wasn't I? 15 or? 16? Yeah
And I've never figured I'd ever record with him and do all the things I did with him later in years, you know, being a New Yorker
